en.help.title: Deno Language Server (deno lsp)
en.help.message:
Deno's language server provides completion, diagnostics, hover, navigation and formatting for TypeScript and JavaScript.

Install the Deno runtime first:
  curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh
  brew install deno

How gvim chooses deno lsp:
  * Native auto-selection (core behaviour, not this helper plugin): when the probed workspace root (the root gvim opened or switched to) has deno.json/deno.jsonc, the runtime is confirmed through the workspace authority under the workspace trust gate (the gate may refuse the probe), lsp_enabled is true and the language is typescript/javascript, core selects deno lsp. It only applies to an LSP manager created for that exact workspace root; nested/per-file TS/JS roots keep their configured server.
  * The selection is a per-root provider; installing or clearing it never stops a running server. An explicit Start/Restart LSP Server for typescript/javascript applies the completed current-root selection to an existing manager: gvim replaces the whole language server list and restarts only that language's servers (other languages and universal servers are untouched); the same explicit action restores the configured baseline when the selection was cleared. Both replacing and same-config Restart preflight the spawn gate before stopping: refusal preserves running servers/config, but preflight→launch is non-transactional — old servers may be stopped and the new start refused when the spawn gate denies, though under Restricted a system-installed binary outside the project may still start; repeated Start of a running server returns the live handle without spawning or gating, even when Blocked; missing-binary/initialize failures are not transactional.
  * When a whole-language replacement is needed, Restart Server on any row of that language replaces the entire server list with the current selection — the clicked row's name is not used in that branch. A root-wide LSP Restart rebuilds managers, and the selection applies when the root creates the next one; explicit Start/Restart launches the auto_start: false deno server.
  * Explicit configuration wins and opts out: an lsp entry for typescript/javascript, a disabled language, or lsp_enabled:false skips Deno auto-selection; tsx is untouched. Settings Save/Reload pushes the reloaded config's server baseline into the LSP port: future managers and the next explicit Start/Restart use it (including a newly added explicit TS/JS server), but the reload itself does not rebuild or restart a running manager — it keeps its old config until that explicit action. Deno auto-selection is not applied while an explicit/disabled entry is present. Trust gates live: reload and revoke/restore pass the LSP config gate before the baseline (the Deno probe shares it); Restricted/Blocked cannot gain auto-starting servers, and after a revoke an already-created manager's old AutoStart configs do not start servers on Open (running ones are not stopped); manual Start/Restart stays allowed. Auto-start and launch spawn are two live checks, not atomic: a revoke between them refuses only when the spawn gate denies (Blocked, remote workspace not Trusted, or a project-contained executable); under Restricted a system-installed binary outside the project may still start. A revoke after the spawn gate passes can likewise let that in-flight start proceed. Neither check nor revoke stops an existing process; later Opens do not auto-start after a revoke.
  * The authority probe requires a strictly clean exit 0: only a successful check (exit 0, no timeout or signal) counts; failures, timeouts, signals, start errors, cancellations or a disconnected authority select nothing; a reconnect re-probes.
  * This bundled plugin's toggle only controls its copy/check/help commands; it does not control native auto-selection, which runs in core regardless of plugin load/enable.
  * Check Project runs deno --version through the workspace authority; the local-only PATH lookup is never used for a presence decision.

Docs: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/getting_started/installation/
en.actions.check: Check project and deno on the workspace
en.status.version_failed: Found %{config} in %{root}, but deno --version did not exit successfully (%{error}), so the project cannot be reported ready. Fix the Deno runtime on the workspace host, then run Deno: Check Project again: %{install} (see Deno: Language Server Help).
en.status.version_failed_no_config: deno --version did not exit successfully on the workspace (%{error}), so Deno is not usable and there is no deno.json or deno.jsonc in %{root}; the project cannot be reported ready. Fix the Deno runtime on the workspace host: %{install} (see Deno: Language Server Help).
